facts.raw_span: A 64-year-old white man was admitted in March 2016 with acute-onset abdominal pain and anemia
acute-onset abdominal pain
anemia
hemoglobin level of 4.4 mmol/L
no weight loss, fever, or constitutional symptoms
α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels within normal ranges
subcapsular hepatic bleeding
active bleeding from one of the two hypervascular lesions in segment IV
two hypervascular liver lesions in segment IV
histologically proven adenoma without malignancy
hypervascular lesions with central necrosis
suspicion for an atypical hepatocellular carcinoma
A 64-year-old white man was admitted in March 2016 with acute-onset abdominal pain and anemia
acute-onset abdominal pain
anemia
hemoglobin level of 4.4 mmol/L
no weight loss, fever, or constitutional symptoms
α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels within normal ranges
subcapsular hepatic bleeding
active bleeding from one of the two hypervascular lesions in segment IV
two hypervascular liver lesions in segment IV
histologically proven adenoma without malignancy
hypervascular lesions with central necrosis
suspicion for an atypical hepatocellular carcinoma

concepts.why: The patient has a history of hypervascular liver lesions in segment IV, which were biopsied and shown to be adenomas without malignancy, and now presents with subcapsular hepatic bleeding and active bleeding from one of the lesions.
The patient has hypervascular liver lesions with central necrosis and a suspicion for atypical hepatocellular carcinoma, which is supported by the presence of liver lesions and bleeding.

concepts.preferred_label: Gastrointestinal Bleeding due to Liver Lesion
concepts.why: The patient presents with acute-onset abdominal pain and anemia, which are consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding, and the bleeding is found to be coming from a liver lesion.
The patient presents with severe anemia and hemodynamic stability, which are consistent with hemorrhagic shock.
The patient is on therapeutic anticoagulation, which increases the risk of bleeding, and presents with bleeding from a liver lesion.
The patient has a history of hypervascular liver lesions in segment IV, which are consistent with the current presentation.

concepts.preferred_label: Abdominal Pain due to Liver Lesion
concepts.why: The patient presents with acute-onset abdominal pain, which is consistent with bleeding from a liver lesion.
The patient presents with severe anemia, which is consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding from a liver lesion.

rationales.F01: Acute-onset abdominal pain and anemia suggest a liver lesion with hemorrhage.
rationales.F04: A low hemoglobin level indicates significant blood loss, consistent with hemorrhage from a liver lesion.
rationales.F07: Subcapsular hepatic bleeding is consistent with a liver lesion with hemorrhage.
rationales.F08: Active bleeding from a hypervascular liver lesion is consistent with a liver lesion with hemorrhage.
rationales.F10: Histologically proven adenoma without malignancy suggests a benign liver lesion.
